newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Nov 27.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Nov 27.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:

** Indian shares likely to drop sharply after the country's top cement maker announces a 56 percent fall in first half net profit. ACC shares seen volatile after falling 11.8 percent in offmarket kerb deals late on Tuesday.
ACC said its net profit fell to 550.5 million rupees in the six months to September 30, 1996 against 1.25 billion rupees.

** Partners of India's coalition government sharply criticise Finance Minister P. Chidambaram for saying the government was considering raising the prices of petroleum products. Left-wing parties in the government fear price rises will hit the working class
** The Hindustan Times newspaper says some parliamentary members of the Congress party have demanded that former Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao step down as Congress Parliament Party (CPP) leader.
Rao made clear he would not quit the CPP post unless MPs calling for him to go, won a two-thirds majority in the CPP.
** The Economic Times says financial institutions (FIs) have asked the finance ministry to make consolidation of accounts among group companies mandatory

** Central bank (RBI) reduces cut-off yield for five-year government stock by 20 basis points to 13.55 percent in its 20 billion rupee auction of five-year paper. About 23 percent of the amount auctioned devolved on the RBI
** Business Standard newspaper says the finance ministry has agreed in principal to a proposal to remove the cash reserve ratio (CRR) requirement on interbank loan transactions.
The move is aimed at pushing down interest rates, which has been an area of concern for the government.
** Telecom firm BPL Cellular Holdings postpones pricing of its issue of American Depositary Receipt (ADR) for the second time to sometime next week, newspapers say
** Indian rupee opens at 35.69/70 per dollar against the previous close of 35.68/69, dealers say

** Moody's Investors Service says it upgrades the bank financial strength rating (BFSR) of Bank of India to D from E+ in recognition of the progress the bank has made in implementing new strategies, including a reorganization of the bank based on consultant's recommendations.
MARKETS:
** Indian shares end mixed on Tuesday after see-sawing wildly in a session driven by punters, traders say
** Bombay's benchmark stocks index closes 46.54 points or 1.55 percent down at 2948.44
** The 50-stocks index of National Stock Exchange (NSE) ends 3.26 points lower at 848.74.
STOCKS TO WATCH:
** Shares of NOCIL, Indian Hotels, GE Shipping, ACC and Colgate likely to see price fluctuations after first half results on Tuesday
** Earnings announcements later today from Essar Shipping, Britannia Industries, Lloyds Steel and Nippon Denro.

** Leading commercial bank State Bank of India likely to double net profit in first half to September 30, 1996. SBI's net is likely to jump to 5.5 billion to six billion rupees from 2.3 billion a year ago, the Business Standard says
